brandon.bio: Brandon Menard, professionally known as CyberDreadx, is an American music producer, AI developer, and blockchain innovator based in Miami. As the founder of Rougee and RougeCoin, he’s building the next-generation music platform that merges Web3 ownership, streaming, and creator empowerment. With a background in AI and cybersecurity, Brandon leads the technical vision and development of Rougee’s decentralized ecosystem, bridging art, tech, and freedom of expression.

andersen.bio: Andersen Scherberger is a veteran music industry professional with over 15 years of experience. He founded a “Best of Miami” award-winning nightclub, hosted countless festivals and events, and managed artists who have performed at major festivals like EDC. His NFT Gallery was featured on CBS’ Destination Miami and solidified partnerships with major crypto brands like Near, Bored Ape Yacht Club, and NFT.com.

elijah.role: Chairman, Miami-Dade County Cryptocurrency Task Force
elijah.bio: Elijah John Bowdre chairs the Miami-Dade County Cryptocurrency Task Force and is president and co-founder of the US Crypto Policy Alliance. He authored Florida’s first state blockchain bill, Miami-Dade County’s Blockchain Board ordinance and the City of Miami’s crypto payment policy, hosts the crypto news show TheBitPoint, and was a candidate for Mayor of Miami in 2025.

teresa.bio: Teresa Castagnino is CEO and co-founder of Like Group Management, a Tulum-based accelerator and incubator focused on regenerative projects, co-founder of Tulum Crypto Fest, and Head of Forbes México for the Caribbean. With a background in industrial design and architecture, she connects founders, businesses and investors across the Mayan Riviera.

ghulam.bio: Dr. Ghulam Abbas is a digital marketing strategist and project manager with a background in healthcare as a qualified homeopathic physician (DHMS) and founder of Eco Cure Clinic. He combines data-driven digital strategy, search-optimized content and cross-functional project management with professional medical knowledge, focusing on organic audience growth, brand positioning and streamlined operational workflows that deliver sustainable, measurable results.

brenda.bio: Brenda Miranda is a multimedia journalist and anchor at Caplin News at Florida International University and a media contributor at the Kopenhaver Center for Women in Communication. Now based in Tulum, she covers community, wellness, the arts and human-interest stories. She graduates from FIU this fall with a bachelor’s degree in digital communication and media.

architecture.title:
One identity.
Independent applications.
architecture.lead: Shared foundations connect the ecosystem. Each application owns its routes, deployment and release cycle.

beyond.title: Different questions. Clear destinations.
beyond.note: The marketing navigation introduces the project. Apps groups applications under Hold, Trade, Play, Talk and Explore. Local navigation belongs to the current dApp. The workspace launcher opens applications plus tools such as Build, Security and Network.

wallet.title: One identity. A reviewed provider boundary.
wallet.lead: Each dApp consumes a common wallet-provider contract rather than owning private keys itself.
wallet.caption: Conceptual production architecture. Final provider and security design belongs to the lead developer.
wallet.demonstrates1: WalletProvider shares the real browser wallet across routes and workspace previews, through @rougechain/core: the same storage keys, vault format and signing as the current rougechain.io.
wallet.demonstrates2: It is single-origin: this does not prove cross-origin wallet connectivity for separately hosted apps.
wallet.evaluate1: RougeChain browser extension, Qwalla and an authoritative web wallet origin are provider candidates.
wallet.evaluate2: Connection, account/network state and transaction permissions need a reviewed contract. No signing or transaction methods are implemented here.
wallet.note: localStorage does not cross origins/subdomains. The future provider strategy must not attempt to share raw vault storage between dApps. Preserve access to existing vaults until a deliberate migration is approved.

boundaries.title: Share the language. Own the product.
boundaries.showcase: Showcase owns the ecosystem registry, routes and workspace previews.
boundaries.walletProvider: @rougechain/wallet-provider requires a separately approved trust and origin architecture.
boundaries.independent: Independent deployments consume versioned packages. No shared runtime server is required for this POC.

transition.title: Move deliberately.

steps.1: Adopt shared brand and UI tokens in one existing surface.
steps.2: Extract the app shell and navigation registry with ownership agreed.
steps.3: Pilot Explorer on its own host with verified data contracts.
steps.4: Move Swap only after wallet, signing and origin boundaries are approved.
steps.5: Redirect old paths only after each destination is deployed and stable.

transition.note: The global switcher crosses applications and hosts. Local navigation stays inside the current application. POC routes demonstrate these boundaries on one origin.
transition.origin: localStorage is origin-scoped. Wallet material on rougechain.io will not automatically transfer to wallet.rougechain.io. A wallet-provider design, migration policy and security review are required before any split. This POC never reads or stores wallet material.
